title: Chess Pieces with Human Feelings
body: Aron Nimzowitsch, a famous chess master, had a very unusual way of describing his games. Instead of treating his pieces like lifeless blocks of wood, he imagined them as living characters with real emotions. He once explained a strategic move by saying the pieces were showing appreciation and friendliness toward one another for their mutual help.

variants.lucy: A grandmaster named Aron looked closely at his wooden figures and saw a tiny world of feelings. He believed the shapes on the board could feel happy and supportive. When they stood side-by-side to protect a square, he said they were showing sweet appreciation for each other's help.
variants.luca: Aron treated his chess games like wild, living adventures. Instead of plain game pieces, his army was full of brave teammates who celebrated every victory. When they teamed up to secure a spot, Aron said they were shouting out loud thanks and showing true friendship on the board.
variants.cn: 有一位特级大师，名叫阿伦。他凑近看自己的木头棋子，竟看见了一个小小的感情世界。他相信棋盘上的这些小家伙会开心，也会互相打气。当它们肩并肩守住一个格子时，他说，它们是在甜甜地感谢对方帮了自己的忙呢。
